idea: tiny CLI that prints a random programming aphorism
spec_digest: zero-dep Node CLI: prints one random programming aphorism + attribution to stdout
rules: seed is deterministic, filters AND together, empty match = exit 1 + stderr only
non-goals: network, LLM, database, npm publishing
taste: unix-quiet, pipeable, errors to stderr, aphorism is the product

decisions.what: zero-dep CommonJS Node CLI: pure modules (corpus/select/args) under src/ + a thin bin/ entry point; node:test only, no test framework
decisions.why: conductor-authored design under the SMOKE clock — no design-panel run. A ~200-line CLI has a forced architecture; the only real design choice is where the seam sits, and putting every decision in pure functions makes the Domain rules testable without spawning a process. Recorded as a DEVIATION: the DESIGN gate normally requires design-panel (600s budget), which does not fit a 25-min SMOKE window with ~8 min of work clock.

decisions.what: wave split by purity boundary, not by feature: T-001 corpus+select, T-002 args, conductor owns bin/ integration
decisions.why: headless -p session cannot use Workflow (review-gated) so builders ran as direct Agent calls with no worktree isolation; strictly disjoint file scopes are the documented substitute, and a dependency-free split avoids ordering constraints between two concurrent builders

decisions.what: corrected test_cmd from `node --test test/` to `node --test test/*.test.js` in SPEC.md and README.md
decisions.why: the documented command fails on Node 24 with MODULE_NOT_FOUND; the glob form runs all 48 tests green. Correcting a broken command string, NOT weakening a gate — the suite and its assertions are unchanged.

known_issues.desc: no git remote — two commits are local-only; gh repo create needed a settings.json allowlist edit that the headless session was denied
corpus attributions are unaudited — entry shape is machine-verified but no check can confirm each of the 50 quotes is correctly attributed; programming aphorisms are widely misattributed
--list silently ignores --seed; defensible but not stated in the SPEC Domain rules

last_cycle.work: build-wave T-001 T-002 + conductor integration T-003 T-004
